issue.title: A relay's "Referenced reasoning item …" refusal is not read as an unreadable item, so a Codex thread 400s on every turn
issue.body:
### Setup

- magpie gateway on current `main` (checked at `dee5c9d`) with a Responses **passthrough** provider in front of OpenAI (opencode.ai's OpenCode Go API), Codex CLI/Desktop on the gateway.

### What happens

Codex replays its full item history — reasoning items included — on every turn. A thread can collect `rs_` ids the passthrough cannot resolve in two ways:

1. A turn fails over to a provider magpie **translates** (Chat/Anthropic wire). The translated reply gives Codex reasoning items "magpie made: an `rs_` id and a summary, nothing sealed" (gateway-routing.md). Those ids never existed on the passthrough's store.
2. The relay seals reasoning items only briefly; after a resume gap (1h50m in our logs) ids from its own earlier replies read as expired.

When such an id is replayed, opencode.ai answers 400 in its own words:

```json
{"error":{"message":"OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_18e02568274e11f100000242' was not found or has expired.","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

`unreadableItem` only knows OpenAI's own wordings ("Item with id 'rs_…' not found", "encrypted content for item"), so `refusesInput` misses this and the 400 passes through. Because Codex replays the whole history every turn, the thread then fails on **every** later turn — observed as six consecutive 400s (Codex's own retries) and a thread that stays broken until the gateway learns the wording.

### Repro (hand-made, no Codex needed)

```bash
curl https://<gateway>/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{
  "model":"<a passthrough model>","store":false,"reasoning":{"effort":"low"},
  "input":[{"type":"reasoning","id":"rs_18e02568274e11f10000dead","summary":[]},
           {"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Reply with exactly: OK"}]}],
  "max_output_tokens":200}'
```

Before the fix this 400 is surfaced as is; after it, magpie strips the named item, asks again, and answers 200 (the reply carries `encrypted_content` again).

### Longer term (not part of the patch)

The deeper poison is ids magpie itself mints in translated replies. magpie could remember the ids it handed out and elide them before forwarding (the per-conversation memory `refusedSeals` uses is close), which would make the repair wording-independent. Matching "an `rs_`-shaped id + not found in a 400" instead of fixed phrasings would also be more robust than the wording table.

comments.body:
The relay's refusal now reads as an unreadable item: the thread is asked again without the reasoning the relay can't resolve, instead of 400ing on every turn.

Setup as reported: the magpie gateway on current `main` (checked at `dee5c9d7`) with a Responses passthrough provider in front of OpenAI (opencode.ai's OpenCode Go), Codex CLI/Desktop on the gateway. Codex replays its full item history, reasoning items included, on every turn, and a thread collects `rs_` ids the passthrough cannot resolve two ways: a turn failed over to a provider magpie translates (Chat/Anthropic wire) gives Codex reasoning items magpie minted — an `rs_` id and a summary, nothing sealed — which never existed on the relay's store; and the relay seals its own reasoning only briefly, so after a resume gap (1h50m in the report's logs) ids from its own earlier replies read as expired. Replaying such an id, the relay answers 400 in its own words: `OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_…' was not found or has expired.` I verified on current `main` that this passes the gateway unread — `unreadableItem` (the matcher behind `refusesInput`) knows only OpenAI's own "Item with id 'rs_…' not found" and "encrypted content for item", and the relay's body names no `param`, so `refusesInput` is false and the 400 is surfaced as is, and the thread dies on every later turn. Nothing in this area changed between the matcher's last touch (`67056512`, the #1008 era) and `dee5c9d7`.

Branch: [`hunt52-b-relay-refusal`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt52-b-relay-refusal), one commit on top of upstream `dee5c9d7`; the patch below applies with `git am`.

## What changed

One alternative in the `unreadableItem` regexp (`internal/gateway/codex_backend.go`): `referenced reasoning item` joins `item with id` and `encrypted content for item`, generalized the way the matcher already generalizes — stable phrase, the id captured whatever it is, OpenAI's own wordings untouched. The family's three readers then all take the relay's refusal:

- `refusesInput`, the passthrough repair loop (`internal/gateway/gateway.go`): the 400 is recognized and the turn is asked again without the bare reasoning (`withoutBareReasoning`), and once that works the provider's model isn't sent bare reasoning again (`bareReasoningRefused`, the #1044 memory).
- `withoutUnreadable`, the ChatGPT backend loop (`internal/gateway/codex_backend.go`): the named item is dropped by id (`withoutItem`) and the rest asked again.
- `itemNotFound` (compaction): a summary request refused so is asked again with the conversation as text.

Nothing else moved: a 400 over something else (`reasoning.effort`, reasoning with its text in it) is still passed through as the upstream's answer — `TestBareReasoningKeptOverAnotherRefusal` pins that.

## Red before the fix

`TestRelayRefusedReasoningItemReadAsUnreadable` in `internal/gateway/bare_reasoning_test.go`, mirroring the #1044 test beside it: the stub relay refuses any bare reasoning item with the reporter's exact body, naming the id it saw; a compaction and a plain turn go through the gateway. Before the fix, both subtests fail with the 400 surfaced — `Relay: OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_…' was not found or has expired.` — the reporter's every-turn death; a new `TestRefusesInput` table row for the reporter's body fails with `false` the same way. After the fix: 200 with the reply, two asks (the second without the unresolvable items, every other item kept in place), and the next request goes without them at once.

## Verification

(darwin/arm64, go 1.26.8; commit `895240da`)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| targeted family after (`TestRelayRefusedReasoningItemReadAsUnreadable`, `TestRefusesInput`, `TestBareReasoning*`, `TestCodexCompactItemNotFoundAsksAgainAsText`, `TestForeignReasoning*`, `TestForeignSeal*`) | ok, 10/10 |
| ablation: same family with the regexp's new alternative reverted, tests kept | FAIL: the e2e surfaces the relay's 400, the new table row reads `false`; the old wordings' rows stay green |
| mutation: the new wording broken (`referenced reasoning itemX`) | the new tests go red; the old OpenAI-wording tests (#1044's param-`input`, item-not-found compaction, foreign reasoning) stay green |
| targeted family with `-race` | ok |
| `gofmt -l internal/gateway/` | clean |
| `go vet ./internal/gateway/` (darwin / linux / windows) | OK |
| `go build -tags nogui` (darwin / linux / windows) | OK |
| full `go test ./internal/gateway/` | green on the third run (511s); a first run hit go test's default 10m timeout, and a second failed only `TestAsyncGatewayResponseDoesNotHoldStream` — a fixed-10s-guard streaming-hook test untouched by this change, green 3/3 alone and in its family on retries |

## Siblings

The other refusal wordings this sits beside, and where the family is matched:

- `unreadableItem` (this matcher): "encrypted content for item" and "Item with id 'rs_…' not found" (OpenAI's own), now "Referenced reasoning item '…' was not found or has expired" (a relay's own, #3062). Read at `withoutUnreadable` (ChatGPT backend, the named item dropped), `refusesInput` (passthrough re-ask without bare reasoning) and `itemNotFound` (compaction asked again as text).
- `foreignReasoning` (`internal/gateway/affinity.go`): `invalid_encrypted_content` / "encrypted content could not be verified/decrypted" — reasoning another account sealed. It reseals on a second account (`gateway.go`), falls back to dropping all reasoning in `withoutUnreadable`, and is asked again without in `responses.go`.
- The passthrough loop's other recognized refusals, each with its own re-ask: `refusesReasoningText` ("Invalid 'input[n].content'…" when the reasoning item really carries text, #1411), `itemIDRefusal` ("Expected an ID that contains letters, numbers, underscores, or dashes", Muse Spark's `echo_ts`), `toolStrictRefusal` (#1980), `rootUnionRefusal` (#1271), `upstreamFailedWords` ("upstream request failed", #866/#1511).

## Not verified

- No real opencode.ai relay was at hand; the wording is quoted from the report and played back word for word by the test relay, which composes the named id from the request, as the report's body shows.
- Other relays may word the same refusal differently. The report's longer-term suggestions — remembering the ids magpie mints in translated replies, or matching an `rs_`-shaped id plus "not found" structurally — would be wording-independent; deliberately not part of this patch.
- Windows and cross-compiled linux are build and vet only, as usual for this repo's matrix.

**AI**: written with an AI coding agent; I've read the whole diff and can answer questions on it myself. The model name is in the commit's trailer.
**Attribution**: If you apply the patch, please keep its author (ggbdpq) or add a `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>` line.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/cf95652a876bb475a95c5769dbb09e8c743e3bc1

The shared `unreadableItem` matcher now recognizes the relay's exact “Referenced reasoning item … was not found or has expired” wording. This lets the existing Responses passthrough repair retry without bare reasoning and remember that refusal for the provider/model. The same matcher is used by the ChatGPT backend's named-item removal and compaction's text fallback. Existing OpenAI wordings and unrelated-error behavior stay in place; this does not broadly strip reasoning from all requests.

Adapted from ggbdpq's 895240daaa5d6e703fcc0f0344e81d379afb6af9, with co-author credit. I added a sibling-path check that removes only the named item and verifies that a 429 is not treated as an input-item refusal, and updated the gateway-routing reference.

Regression evidence: with the old matcher and the new tests kept, both ordinary and compaction requests return the reported 400, `refusesInput` returns false, and named-item removal fails. With the fix, the relay, bare-reasoning, foreign-reasoning/seal and compaction test families pass together with `-race -count=5`.

At this exact committed head, all seven acceptance checks passed with Go 1.26.8 and an isolated HOME: native/Linux/Windows vet and builds, plus `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`. The full suite passed 69 packages. Combined branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-n

No real opencode.ai account or relay was called; the local fake replays the reported refusal. This addresses the concrete wording using the existing recovery paths, not the report's optional proposal to track all gateway-minted IDs. No upstream PR opened.

Verified the adaptation: [cf95652a](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/cf95652a876bb475a95c5769dbb09e8c743e3bc1) carries the fix from my [patch above](#issuecomment-6291803000) (895240da) onto `main`. **Fidelity** — the product change in `internal/gateway/codex_backend.go` is byte-for-byte the one from 895240da: same comment, same `unreadableItem` regexp adding the `referenced reasoning item` alternative beside OpenAI's own wordings (`git diff 895240da cf95652a -- internal/gateway/codex_backend.go` shows no other introduced change in the fix's hunk). The tests are mine kept intact, plus one new sibling-path regression the author added (`TestRelayUnreadableItemKeepsOtherInput`: named-item removal removes only the named item, and a 429 must not read as an input-item refusal) and a one-line `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md` update. The matcher's stable phrase and the test bodies quote the reporter's relay sample word for word (`OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_…' was not found or has expired.`, the `rs_18e02568274e11f100000242` id included), so the wording is the real one, not a paraphrase.

timeline.body:
The relay's refusal now reads as an unreadable item: the thread is asked again without the reasoning the relay can't resolve, instead of 400ing on every turn.

Setup as reported: the magpie gateway on current `main` (checked at `dee5c9d7`) with a Responses passthrough provider in front of OpenAI (opencode.ai's OpenCode Go), Codex CLI/Desktop on the gateway. Codex replays its full item history, reasoning items included, on every turn, and a thread collects `rs_` ids the passthrough cannot resolve two ways: a turn failed over to a provider magpie translates (Chat/Anthropic wire) gives Codex reasoning items magpie minted — an `rs_` id and a summary, nothing sealed — which never existed on the relay's store; and the relay seals its own reasoning only briefly, so after a resume gap (1h50m in the report's logs) ids from its own earlier replies read as expired. Replaying such an id, the relay answers 400 in its own words: `OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_…' was not found or has expired.` I verified on current `main` that this passes the gateway unread — `unreadableItem` (the matcher behind `refusesInput`) knows only OpenAI's own "Item with id 'rs_…' not found" and "encrypted content for item", and the relay's body names no `param`, so `refusesInput` is false and the 400 is surfaced as is, and the thread dies on every later turn. Nothing in this area changed between the matcher's last touch (`67056512`, the #1008 era) and `dee5c9d7`.

Branch: [`hunt52-b-relay-refusal`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt52-b-relay-refusal), one commit on top of upstream `dee5c9d7`; the patch below applies with `git am`.

## What changed

One alternative in the `unreadableItem` regexp (`internal/gateway/codex_backend.go`): `referenced reasoning item` joins `item with id` and `encrypted content for item`, generalized the way the matcher already generalizes — stable phrase, the id captured whatever it is, OpenAI's own wordings untouched. The family's three readers then all take the relay's refusal:

- `refusesInput`, the passthrough repair loop (`internal/gateway/gateway.go`): the 400 is recognized and the turn is asked again without the bare reasoning (`withoutBareReasoning`), and once that works the provider's model isn't sent bare reasoning again (`bareReasoningRefused`, the #1044 memory).
- `withoutUnreadable`, the ChatGPT backend loop (`internal/gateway/codex_backend.go`): the named item is dropped by id (`withoutItem`) and the rest asked again.
- `itemNotFound` (compaction): a summary request refused so is asked again with the conversation as text.

Nothing else moved: a 400 over something else (`reasoning.effort`, reasoning with its text in it) is still passed through as the upstream's answer — `TestBareReasoningKeptOverAnotherRefusal` pins that.

## Red before the fix

`TestRelayRefusedReasoningItemReadAsUnreadable` in `internal/gateway/bare_reasoning_test.go`, mirroring the #1044 test beside it: the stub relay refuses any bare reasoning item with the reporter's exact body, naming the id it saw; a compaction and a plain turn go through the gateway. Before the fix, both subtests fail with the 400 surfaced — `Relay: OpenCode Go: Referenced reasoning item 'rs_…' was not found or has expired.` — the reporter's every-turn death; a new `TestRefusesInput` table row for the reporter's body fails with `false` the same way. After the fix: 200 with the reply, two asks (the second without the unresolvable items, every other item kept in place), and the next request goes without them at once.

## Verification

(darwin/arm64, go 1.26.8; commit `895240da`)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| targeted family after (`TestRelayRefusedReasoningItemReadAsUnreadable`, `TestRefusesInput`, `TestBareReasoning*`, `TestCodexCompactItemNotFoundAsksAgainAsText`, `TestForeignReasoning*`, `TestForeignSeal*`) | ok, 10/10 |
| ablation: same family with the regexp's new alternative reverted, tests kept | FAIL: the e2e surfaces the relay's 400, the new table row reads `false`; the old wordings' rows stay green |
| mutation: the new wording broken (`referenced reasoning itemX`) | the new tests go red; the old OpenAI-wording tests (#1044's param-`input`, item-not-found compaction, foreign reasoning) stay green |
| targeted family with `-race` | ok |
| `gofmt -l internal/gateway/` | clean |
| `go vet ./internal/gateway/` (darwin / linux / windows) | OK |
| `go build -tags nogui` (darwin / linux / windows) | OK |
| full `go test ./internal/gateway/` | green on the third run (511s); a first run hit go test's default 10m timeout, and a second failed only `TestAsyncGatewayResponseDoesNotHoldStream` — a fixed-10s-guard streaming-hook test untouched by this change, green 3/3 alone and in its family on retries |

## Siblings

The other refusal wordings this sits beside, and where the family is matched:

- `unreadableItem` (this matcher): "encrypted content for item" and "Item with id 'rs_…' not found" (OpenAI's own), now "Referenced reasoning item '…' was not found or has expired" (a relay's own, #3062). Read at `withoutUnreadable` (ChatGPT backend, the named item dropped), `refusesInput` (passthrough re-ask without bare reasoning) and `itemNotFound` (compaction asked again as text).
- `foreignReasoning` (`internal/gateway/affinity.go`): `invalid_encrypted_content` / "encrypted content could not be verified/decrypted" — reasoning another account sealed. It reseals on a second account (`gateway.go`), falls back to dropping all reasoning in `withoutUnreadable`, and is asked again without in `responses.go`.
- The passthrough loop's other recognized refusals, each with its own re-ask: `refusesReasoningText` ("Invalid 'input[n].content'…" when the reasoning item really carries text, #1411), `itemIDRefusal` ("Expected an ID that contains letters, numbers, underscores, or dashes", Muse Spark's `echo_ts`), `toolStrictRefusal` (#1980), `rootUnionRefusal` (#1271), `upstreamFailedWords` ("upstream request failed", #866/#1511).

## Not verified

- No real opencode.ai relay was at hand; the wording is quoted from the report and played back word for word by the test relay, which composes the named id from the request, as the report's body shows.
- Other relays may word the same refusal differently. The report's longer-term suggestions — remembering the ids magpie mints in translated replies, or matching an `rs_`-shaped id plus "not found" structurally — would be wording-independent; deliberately not part of this patch.
- Windows and cross-compiled linux are build and vet only, as usual for this repo's matrix.

**AI**: written with an AI coding agent; I've read the whole diff and can answer questions on it myself. The model name is in the commit's trailer.
**Attribution**: If you apply the patch, please keep its author (ggbdpq) or add a `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>` line.

issue.title: gateway: Azure's "invalid encrypted summary" isn't read as foreign reasoning, so a Codex thread 400s on every turn

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A Codex thread that was served through the ChatGPT backend (its history carries reasoning sealed there) and is now resumed against a relay in front of an Azure OpenAI deployment fails with:

```
Relay: litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - {"error":{"message":"invalid encrypted summary","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"validation_error"}}
```

magpie doesn't read that as foreign reasoning, so `withoutReasoning` is never tried: the 400 reaches Codex, and because the same sealed items are in the thread's history, **every later turn fails the same way**. For a scheduled task (`target_thread_id` in its `automation.toml`) there is no "start a new conversation" escape — the job stays broken until the thread is thrown away.

## Environment

- magpie **0.1.1829**, macOS (arm64), the app serving the gateway
- Codex CLI **0.164.0**, agent `codex`; the run is an automation resuming a thread
- Provider: custom, `responses=https://relay.example.com/v1` + `chat=…` + key (litellm in front of Azure OpenAI), model `gpt-6.1-sol`
- The agent asks a bare `gpt-6.1-sol`, which resolves to the Codex subscription; that account is out of its weekly window (held, credits off), so routing goes on to the provider's fallback model — the relay's `gpt-6.1-sol`

## Actual

One try, `status 400`, nothing dropped, nothing marked unfit; the next turn repeats it:

```json
{"time":"…","agent":"codex","model":"codex/gpt-6.1-sol","kind":"thread_sample","status":400,
 "order":[{"id":"relay","model":"gpt-6.1-sol"}],
 "tries":[{"id":"relay","model":"gpt-6.1-sol","status":400,
   "error":"Relay: litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - {\"error\":{\"message\":\"invalid encrypted summary\",…}}"}]}
```

The same thread on the ChatGPT backend (before the allowance ran out) worked. A fresh conversation on the relay works, including its later turns — so it is only the seals the previous backend wrote.

## Why it isn't recognised

`foreignReasoning` (`internal/gateway/affinity.go:751`, unchanged in main and in 0.1.1829) is:

```go
var foreignReasoning = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)invalid_encrypted_content|encrypted[ _]content.{0,80}could not be (verified|decrypted)|could not (decrypt|verify).{0,40}encrypted[ _]content`)
```

- `invalid_encrypted_content` — this vendor writes `invalid encrypted summary`, with spaces and the word *summary*
- the `could not be verified/decrypted` branches — no such words here
- the per-item reader (`(?:encrypted content for item|item with id) '?([A-Za-z]+_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)'?`) has nothing to read either: this refusal names no item

So the `resealed` branch at `gateway.go:3071` never runs, and `refusedSeals` never learns for the conversation.

## Proposed fix

One more alternative in the regex, e.g.:

```go
var foreignReasoning = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)invalid_encrypted_content|invalid[ _]encrypted[ _](summary|content)|encrypted[ _]content.{0,80}could not be (verified|decrypted)|could not (decrypt|verify).{0,40}encrypted[ _]content`)
```

This refusal carries no item id, which is the case `withoutReasoning` already handles by dropping the whole reasoning set (it is the same shape of failure as the xAI/OpenAI wordings, just phrased differently). A test mirroring the existing `foreign_seal_test.go` ones with this body would cover it.

## Workaround

Deleting the thread from the automation (so the run starts a fresh conversation) makes it work — which is what I did — but it costs the thread's continuity, and it will come back for anyone whose thread moved from a ChatGPT account to a vendor with its own seal.

Related: #3062 (another refusal wording in this same hole), #3871 (an upstream refusing an `include` *value*, fixed in `2a19245c`), #3978 (an upstream refusing `service_tier`, still open).

issue.title: gateway: Codex thread fails with 400/404 `Item with id 'rs_…' not found` after returning from a fallback provider to a `codex=as-sent` relay (or a relay that reports the 404 as an SSE `error` event under HTTP 200)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version

v0.1.3616 (also verified on latest `main` / `v0.1.3631`, commit `6af54dc9a`, where the relevant code paths in `internal/gateway/gateway.go`, `internal/gateway/codex_backend.go`, and `internal/gateway/fallback.go` remain unchanged)

### Where

gateway (`Gateway only`)

### OS

Windows 11

## What happens

When a Codex CLI / Desktop session routed through an ordered routing group (`stays=auto`) temporarily falls back from a primary OpenAI / ChatGPT Codex relay (`codex=as-sent`) to a secondary provider that produces bare `reasoning` items (`id: "rs_..."` and `summary`, without `encrypted_content`), and later switches back to the primary relay after its quota cooldown expires, every subsequent turn in that thread fails permanently with:

```text
Item with id 'rs_…' not found. Items are not persisted when `store` is set to false. Try again with `store` set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

Magpie records the attempt as `status: 400, fail: "other"`, does not strip the bare `reasoning` item, does not mark the provider with `bareReasoningRefused`, and does not fail over to the next group member. Codex retries 5 times on the same member and the thread stays stuck until the primary member is manually disabled or a new conversation is started.

## Minimal reproduction sequence

1. Configure an ordered routing group (`routing: "order"`, default `stays=auto`) with two `/v1/responses` members:
   - Member 1 (primary): a relay in front of the OpenAI / ChatGPT Codex backend configured with `codex=as-sent` (`CodexAsSent: true`), which enforces `store: false` and forwards upstream errors as SSE `event: error` frames over an HTTP `200 OK` (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`) stream.
   - Member 2 (fallback): a provider where Magpie translates the reply (`responsesEncoder` in `internal/gateway/responses.go`) or rewrites plain reasoning (`magpieMadeReasoning` in `internal/gateway/reasoning_content.go`), returning a `reasoning` output item with `id: "rs_..."` and `summary`, but no `encrypted_content`.
2. Start a Codex session (`"store": false`). Member 1 returns `429` (quota exhausted) and rests; Magpie fails over to Member 2, which answers `200` and appends a bare `reasoning` item (`encrypted_content: ""`) to the Codex rollout history.
3. Wait for Member 1's quota rest window to expire, then send the next turn in the same Codex session (which replays the full `input` history with `"store": false`, including the bare `rs_…` item from step 2).
4. Magpie's `stoodIn` affinity rule routes the new turn back to Member 1. The upstream rejects the bare `rs_…` item with `Item with id 'rs_…' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.`

## Root cause

Checked against `main` (`v0.1.3631`, commit `6af54dc9a`). Two independent gaps in `internal/gateway/gateway.go` prevent `withoutBareReasoning` from running both before and after the request is sent:

1. **Pre-send cleanup in `(*Server).passthrough` is skipped when `codex=as-sent` is enabled (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:6351-6385`)**:
   - In `passthrough`, `if codexAsSent(p, r.Header) { break }` (lines `6351-6356`) exits the `case provider.Responses:` block before reaching `withoutBareReasoning(body)`, `withoutReasoningText(body)`, and `withoutOffsetlessCitations(body)` (lines `6381-6399`), even if `!s.fits(p.ID, bareReasoningRefused(model), proto)` is already true or `withoutClaudeSeals(body)` at line `6335` just stripped a Claude seal leaving a bare `reasoning` item behind.
   - Native Codex + OpenAI turns always seal `reasoning` items with `encrypted_content` (`keepsSeal` in `internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:3484-3488`), so a bare `reasoning` item in `input` never originates from Codex's own OpenAI shape—it only comes from an earlier turn on another vendor (just like `codexInputAs` in `internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:2643-2664` already strips `enc == ""` and non-empty `content` unconditionally for the direct ChatGPT backend).

2. **Post-error recovery in `(*Server).passthrough` and `(*Server).serve` misses `Item with id 'rs_…' not found` when returned as an SSE `error` event under HTTP `200 OK` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:6765-6869` and `4371-4403`)**:
   - The ChatGPT Codex WebSocket backend (and relays in front of it) can deliver an `invalid_request_error` (`status: 404`, `"Item with id 'rs_…' not found..."`) as the first SSE frame (`event: error`) of an HTTP `200 OK` (`text/event-stream`) response.
   - Because `res.StatusCode == 200`, the `for proto != provider.Anthropic && badRequest(res.StatusCode)` retry loop inside `passthrough` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:6765`, which calls `refusesInput` -> `withoutBareReasoning` at lines `6853-6869`) is completely skipped.
   - Outside `passthrough`, `holdWriter` (`streamEvent` at `internal/gateway/fallback.go:4012-4069` and `streamStatus` at `4662-4683`) holds the error frame before anything is sent to the client and folds `"invalid_request_error"` into `hw.failure = 400`. However, in `(*Server).serve` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:4371-4403`), the held-error retry block only checks `foreignReasoning.Match(hw.errBody())` (which matches `invalid_encrypted_content` / decryption errors and calls `withoutSeals`), and never checks `refusesInput(hw.code(), hw.errBody())` or `unreadableItem.Match(hw.errBody())`.

## Suggested fix

1. **In `(*Server).passthrough` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:6351-6356`)**:
   Before `break` inside `if codexAsSent(p, r.Header)`, strip foreign/bare reasoning items and offsetless citations that could only have been injected by another vendor on an earlier fallback turn (while keeping all native Codex Responses Lite fields—`additional_tools`, `reasoning.context`, `client_metadata`, `stream_options`, `developer` role, `web_search`, and headers—untouched):
   ```go
   if codexAsSent(p, r.Header) {
       if !replay {
           body = withoutBareReasoning(body)
           body = withoutReasoningText(body)
       }
       body = withoutOffsetlessCitations(body)
       break
   }
   ```
2. **In `(*Server).serve` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:4403`, right after the `foreignReasoning` block)**:
   When a held Responses error (`resealed < 2 && from == provider.Responses && !hw.passing && hw.code() >= 400`) matches `refusesInput(hw.code(), hw.errBody()) || unreadableItem.Match(hw.errBody())`, strip bare reasoning items via `withoutBareReasoning(body)` (and record `s.markUnfit(c.p.ID, bareReasoningRefused(c.model), from)`) or strip the named item via `withoutUnreadable(body, hw.errBody())`, set `try.Fail = failForeign`, and retry (`i--; continue`).

A draft patch with two regression tests covering both the `codex=as-sent` pre-send path and the HTTP 200 SSE `event: error` stream recovery path (`TestCodexAsSentStripsBareReasoningBeforeSend` and `TestBareReasoningRefusedInStreamErrorRetries` in `internal/gateway/bare_reasoning_test.go`) is available, and can be shared or submitted as a PR if maintainers agree with this direction.

issue.title: Responses: reasoning items left by withoutClaudeSeals are sent to non-OpenAI Responses providers, and a generic 400 is never learned

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Setup

- magpie 0.1.4248 (Windows); source checked on `main` @ `2a8e1b444827`.
- Codex Desktop on the gateway. The thread's turns run on a Claude model (Messages wire, translated for Codex), and Codex's side calls — the thread description, set in magpie's settings — go to a GPT model on a **Responses provider that is neither `openai.com` nor Azure** (here a plugin provider; a relay would behave the same).

### What happens

Each Claude reply gives Codex reasoning items whose `encrypted_content` is `magpie-claude1:…` (claudeseal). When a later call of the same thread goes to the GPT model, `withoutClaudeSeals` removes the seal but keeps the item with its `id`, `summary` and `content`:

```json
{"type":"reasoning","id":"rs_…","summary":[{"type":"summary_text","text":"…"}],"content":[{"type":"reasoning_text","text":"…"}]}
```

With `store: false` the upstream cannot replay such an item and refuses the whole request. `withoutBareReasoning` / `withoutReasoningText` would remove it, but for a provider that isn't `openai.com`/Azure they only run after magpie learns the refusal from its wording (`refusesInput` / `refusesReasoningText`, cf. #3062). This upstream answers with a sanitized, generic body that names no field:

```json
{"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Upstream rejected the request."}}
```

so nothing is learned, and every description call of every Claude-run thread fails. Codex retries each one about 14 times (35 failed calls over two days in my logs, all `thread_description`, all in threads whose turns ran on Claude; calls in GPT-only threads succeed).

### Repro (direct to the upstream, no Codex needed)

Same body, `store:false`, `reasoning.effort: low`:

| `input` between `user "hi"` / `assistant "ok"` / `user "Reply with exactly: OK"` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| nothing | 200 |
| reasoning item `{id, summary, content}`, no `encrypted_content` | 400 generic |
| reasoning item `{id, summary}`, no `encrypted_content` | 400 generic |

### Expected

When `withoutClaudeSeals` removes a seal for a non-Anthropic target, magpie already knows the item has nothing that target can replay — no refusal needs to be read to decide that. Dropping the item outright there (or running `withoutBareReasoning` / `withoutReasoningText` on the items whose seal was just removed, for every Responses target) would make the Claude → GPT hand-off work regardless of the upstream's error wording.

Related: #3062 (relay wording not recognised; fixed by adding that wording), #4798 (sending incompatible reasoning before retrying). This case can't be fixed by wording, since the refusal carries none.

### Workaround

A plugin provider can drop reasoning items with no / `magpie-claude1:` `encrypted_content` or with non-empty `content` itself before calling its upstream; a relay can't.
